name: On the street
kid: Out on the street there’s no Wi-Fi, so the parcels fly by radio to a cell tower, and from there along a glass thread to the internet.
nerd: On 5G the phone talks NR to a gNB, which tunnels the packets (GTP-U) over fibre to the mobile core; its UPF does carrier-grade NAT towards the internet.

phone.kid: Your phone wants a cat video, even out here. It sends a little request by radio.

cell-tower-internet.kid: From the tower, your parcels travel inside a tunnel along a glass thread to the mobile company.
cell-tower-internet.nerd: Fibre backhaul from the gNB to the core; user packets ride inside GTP-U (UDP 2152) tunnels, one per session.

internet.nerd: The mobile core (5GC) ends the radio tunnel and does carrier-grade NAT; from there it’s the same internet: the ISP core, peering at an IXP (or paid transit), and a CDN cache close to you.
